notes: Summary: POC completed Feb 2026. Initially promising latency and cost profile vs incumbent but lost on end-to-end quality for structured outputs and tool-calls.
Sales rep: Ava Martinez. SE: Rahul Kapoor. Multiple exec touchpoints (CTO, Head of AI, Legal Ops).
Use-case: high-accuracy contract clause extraction + downstream automated contract-edit tool-calling (create amendments, flag clauses). Need strict JSON schema and traceable audit logs.
POC scope: 3-week run with Redwood hosted + Dedicated eval. Compared against incumbent (IncumbentX) which runs in-corp with proprietary tool-calling SDK.
- Latency: Redwood dedicated median 120ms token-step vs incumbent 160ms (Redwood faster).
- Cost: Estimated 35% lower token cost on Redwood's quantized profiles.
- Quality: Incumbent outperformed on structured extraction F1 (incumbent 0.88 vs Redwood 0.74 on contract clause dataset).

- Tool-calling: Redwood's tool-calling had 12% mis-invocation rate on complex amend flows (missing param normalization). Incumbent had 3% due to stricter schema enforcement and custom pre-/post-processors.
Customer quote (Head of AI): 'We liked the economics, but the errors in amendment calls are business-critical — can't ship with that risk.'
- 2026-02-05: Internal security flagged lack of documented JSON schema enforcement and absence of enforced tool-call validation hooks. Jira SEC-4590 opened.
- 2026-02-14: Fireflies call w/ CTO + Rahul + Ava to review failing cases (ff-20260214-CR-91).
- 2026-02-18: Procurement paused — legal requests for on-prem trial and evidence of iso27001 cert from Redwood partner. Budget freeze announced by CFO pending Q2 planning.

Decision: IncumbentX offered a migration path with lower initial change management (their tool-calling tightly integrated with existing RPA). Cobalt Scribe elected to remain with incumbent; formal closed-lost communicated 2026-02-25.
Internal takeaways: need stronger structured-output guarantees (schema enforcement), tool-calling validation hooks, and an enterprise on-prem quickstart for security teams.

Follow-up plan: Archive as closed-lost, watchlist for roadmap milestones (schema enforcement feature, tool-calling reliability improvements). Reconnect in 6-9 months or if legal/ops champion reappears.

use_case_summary: Contract clause extraction and automated amendment tool-calls; requires high-precision structured JSON outputs, low false-invocation of downstream action calls, and full auditability.
requirements_summary: Must support strict schema enforcement for structured outputs, tool-call validation hooks (pre-call param validation + dry-run), enterprise SSO (SAML), SOC2/ISO evidence, ability to run private on-prem pilot for legal/regulatory compliance. Low tolerance for hallucinations in tool-calling flows.
